prompt:
Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten figures of the same character, drawn as copper-plate engravings for a 19th-century book. The first reference image gives the exact layout and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the drawing changes. The first reference is a plain 3D render: take only the layout and the poses from it, never its smooth shading or its plastic 3D look. The second reference image only shows the costume, the face and the proportions of the character: do not copy its drawing style, its colours or its three-view layout. The third reference image shows the engraving technique and line weight of the game: draw the figures with exactly this technique, but do not copy any of its content.

Technique: a copper-plate engraving with etching, printed in a single pure black ink on pure white paper (no tinted ground). Everything is built only from engraved lines: long parallel hatching, cross-hatching in two or three directions for the darks, swelling lines that are thick in the shadows and taper to hair-thin points in the light, short flicks and stipple dots for stone and rock, contour lines that follow the forms. The tone values come only from the thickness and spacing of the lines: no grey wash, no aquatint, no tonal gradients, no airbrush, no smudged pencil shading, no colour; between the lines the paper stays white. A firm, clear contour line around every shape; the hatching curves around the round body, the arms, the legs and the cap; short engraved flicks for the fur. Light from the upper left. The colours of the costume become tone values: the dark fur and the dark face stripes in dense cross-hatching, the white face stripes and the light belly almost bare white paper with a few fine lines, the cream shirt light with sparse hatching, the dark green cap and vest in medium-dark hatching, the red scarf in medium hatching with the knitting hinted by short strokes, the satchel dark, the parcel light with its string clearly drawn. Keep the face clearly readable: a small dark eye with a white highlight, a black nose, the broad stripes of the face. The lines must be bold and clearly separated so that the figure stays readable when shown about 250 pixels tall: about 60 to 80 hatching lines across the height of a figure, never a grey mush. Not a cartoon, not a comic, not a 3D render, not a painting, not a pencil sketch, no colour.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Each figure isolated on a fully transparent background; inside the figure the white paper between the lines is opaque white. Clear empty space between the figures; no ground, no cast shadow, no frame borders, nothing cut off at the edge of the sheet.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

A sheet of three separate printer's ornaments for a 19th-century book, each one a copper-plate engraving printed in a single pure black ink on pure white paper, crisp engraved lines, parallel hatching and cross-hatching, tone only through line thickness and spacing, no grey wash, no colour, no gradients. The three ornaments stand apart from each other with wide white space between them:
1. On the left half: a square decorative initial block, as tall as half of the sheet, with a fine double ruled border line. Inside the border a dense engraved maritime ornament of rope, an anchor, sea waves, seaweed and a small lighthouse, all around a large EMPTY square of plain white paper in the middle (half the width of the block) where a letter will be printed later: the inner square must stay completely empty and white, no letter in it.
2. Top right: a small oval tailpiece vignette: a coil of rope with a small anchor and a gull, finely engraved, fading out at the edges into white paper.
3. Bottom right: a long, thin horizontal ornamental divider rule with a small knot of rope in the middle and swelling, tapering flourishes towards both ends.
No tinted ground, no colour at all. The reference image only shows the engraving technique and the line weight: use the same technique, do not copy any of its content. Not a 3D render, not a painting, not a woodcut, no paper texture, no stains, no frame around the sheet.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

A flat colour-code segmentation map of the reference image, for a game engine. Keep the exact composition, the exact positions, sizes and outlines of everything in the reference image; only replace the drawing by flat, uniform colour areas with hard edges, no lines, no hatching, no shading, no gradients, no anti-aliasing. Colour codes: the whole sky including clouds pure blue #0000FF; all open water of the sea and the harbour pure cyan #00FFFF; the two boats with their masts and rigging pure magenta #FF00FF; the lit window of the cottage pure yellow #FFFF00; the glass of the iron lantern pure orange #FF8000; the lamp at the top of the lighthouse pure red #FF0000; the chimney of the cottage pure green #00FF00; everything else (cottage, lighthouse tower, rocks, jetty, quay, barrels, crates, rope, lantern post) pure black #000000. No text, no labels, no legend. Image format: landscape 3:2.
